findings.title: New abstract order() breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java:44 the interface adds abstract `int order()` with no default. CryptoProvider is a ServiceLoader SPI that third parties can implement outside this repo. Adding an abstract method breaks source and binary compatibility: existing custom providers fail to compile and fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError when loaded. The fix is to provide a default, e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`, so old implementations keep working and the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) still loses to built-ins (order 200).

findings.title: Multiple crypto providers silently resolved instead of failing, tie is nondeterministic
findings.body: In common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java:56 detectProvider now sorts by order() reversed and returns the first, only logging ignored providers at debug. Previously >1 providers threw IllegalStateException. All built-ins DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider now return order 200, so a misconfigured classpath with both FIPS and non-FIPS has a tie resolved by ServiceLoader iteration order, which is undefined. Consequence is silent use of the wrong crypto stack, e.g. running non-FIPS while FIPS compliance was expected, with no visible warning. Should at least throw on equal top orders or log at warn.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns wrong JCA provider
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:61 getBouncyCastleProvider() returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, typically SUN/JKS, not a BouncyCastle provider. The contract is to return the BouncyCastle provider, and WildFlyElytronProvider returns null when there is none. Callers that use this to select BC algorithms, register the provider, or check provider ID will get SUN behavior or mis-identify the stack, causing subtle crypto failures. Should return null or throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unimplemented methods.

findings.title: ECDSA DER-to-raw conversion silently truncates oversized/negative integers
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:151 integerToBytes() does `if (qLength < bytes.length) copy last qLength bytes` with no validation. A DER INTEGER for P-256 (qLength 32) that is 34 bytes long, or a negative INTEGER that new BigInteger(bytes) accepts as signed, is truncated to the low bytes instead of rejected. Only the case bytes.length==qLength+1 with leading 0x00 is valid; larger values or negative values must throw IOException. Silent wrapping maps an invalid attacker-supplied signature to a different valid-looking raw R/S pair, enabling signature malleability and bypass of strict DER checks.

findings.title: Missing validation of raw ECDSA signature length
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:103 concatenatedRSToASN1DER(byte[] signature, int signLength) assumes signature.length==signLength and signLength even without checking, then does System.arraycopy with len=signLength/2. A short buffer throws raw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException/IllegalArgumentException, and a long buffer silently ignores trailing bytes. This produces confusing errors and can hide caller bugs where e.g. a P-521 signature is passed with ES256 length. Must validate signLength>0, even, expected (64/96/132) and signature.length==signLength.

findings.title: ASN.1 SEQUENCE parser does not enforce exact length and accepts non-DER
findings.body: In authz/client/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/util/crypto/ASN1Decoder.java:49 readSequence() loops `while(length>0){length-=bytes.length;}` with no check that final length==0 and no check for trailing bytes, and readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length 0x80 instead of rejecting. A parent length smaller than the children sum goes negative and is still accepted if 2 elements were read, and extra bytes after the SEQUENCE are ignored. DER requires definite lengths and exact consumption. Consequence is acceptance of malformed/non-canonical ECDSA signatures, signature malleability and interop differences versus BouncyCastle/JCA strict parsers.

findings.title: ECDSA test reuses one P-256 key and only checks round-trip
findings.body: In authz/client/src/test/java/org/keycloak/authorization/client/test/ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java:46 the helper generates one EC KeyPair with default curve (P-256) and reuses it for ES256/ES384/ES512, then only asserts decode(encode(decode(sign))) equals decode(sign). It never verifies the DER with Signature.verify nor compares raw/DER against a reference implementation or fixed vectors. A systematically wrong encoder/decoder that is self-consistent still passes, and real 48/66-byte component sizes are never exercised. Should generate P-256/P-384/P-521 keys per algorithm and verify signatures end-to-end.
